- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00 followed by high forecast), especially in early days of the 30d horizon — apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- Mean reversion is evident: if forecast is >20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 15–25% unless sentiment is strong and rising.
- For horizon 30d, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — apply a 3–5 day smoothing window to align with actual price momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 14-day average if sentiment is trending flat or reversing.
